newsitem.title: USA: Manufacturing index slips in September.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing index slips in September.

text.p: Manufacturing growth slowed in September, the nation's purchasing managers said Tuesday in a report pointing to moderating economic expansion ahead.

The National Association of Purchasing Management said its index of manufacturing activity fell to 51.7 last month from 52.6 in August, indicating growth last month was at a slower rate than in August. A reading above 50 points to growth in manufacturing while one below that level signals contraction.
Analysts said the report was another sign that the overall economy would cool off in the third quarter after growing briskly in the second quarter.
"The report shows the manufacturing sector is just muddling through," said Elliott Platt, research director at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette.

In a separate report, the Conference Board said its Index of Leading Indicators, a key economic forecasting gauge, rose 0.2 percent in August after a 0.2 percent gain in July. It was the seventh straight increase and fit with other recent signs of slower but steady growth in the third quarter and beyond.

The purchasing managers' report -- the first broad reading of the economy's performance each month -- came in slightly weaker than had been expected on Wall Street, helping to calm investor worries about a pickup in inflation and fuelling a mild rally in the inflation-sensitive bond market.
The 30-year Treasury rose 15/32, or $4.6875 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.89 percent from 6.92 percent on Monday.
Many economists are forecasting that economic growth slowed to a rate of 2 percent or so in the third quarter from the brisk 4.7 percent pace in the second quarter.

The second quarter's burst of growth kindled worries that inflation would pick up, but the Federal Reserve elected to hold short-term interest rates steady last month, rather than raising rates in a bid to ward off inflation.

In its report, the NAPM said its index of prices paid by manufacturers rose in September for the first time in four months. But faster deliveries from suppliers, which mean less inflationary bottlenecks during production, and weakness in the employment and inventory readings helped offset any worries about inflation, analysts said.
"The inflation signals are basically a wash and the (bond) market is doing better on the soft economic data," said Alan Levenson, money market economist at UBS Securities.

The group's report indicated manufacturing employment fell for the 20th consecutive month, suggesting there was no labour shortage in the industrial sector, analysts said. The lowest unemployment overall in a generation has produced some signs of upward pressure on wages, which could fuel inflation.

"We should have a continuation of little, if any, gain in employment in the manufacturing sector and probably 0.2 or 0.3 percent monthly gains in industrial production in the fourth quarter," Platt said.
The association's members purchase everything from aluminum to cardboard boxes to computer chips for about 300 of the nation's largest corporations.
